rows.claim: The flat vector exists so integrator compatibility (OrdinaryDiffEq or custom), trim solvers, HDF5 logging and linearization all get their arrays
rows.evidence: src/stepper.jl:239 only mentions OrdinaryDiffEqCore as a source of constants; no HDF5 in src/. design/spec.md:6496 drops OrdinaryDiffEq as a dependency, and design/pending.md:264-268 says HDF5 export is undecided.
rows.fix: Integrator backends behind the stepper seam (§10.2), trim solvers and linearization all get their arrays.
rows.note: pending.md:264-268 records this very bullet as awaiting a reword when its deferral lifts. Spec 6730 allows an OrdinaryDiffEq extension later. The flat buffer itself is real (src/checkpoint.jl, src/store.jl).

rows.claim: Gain trajectories (scheduler outputs) become observable in log, trace and replay
rows.evidence: src/trace.jl:1-6 and spec §11.5 (design/spec.md:8754-8763): the trace is the input trace, one record per drained root-input batch. A scheduler's gain bundle is an internal port, written by no device, so no trace record holds it. The log (snapshots) holds it, and replay reproduces it bit-identically (src/sim.jl:1262-1266).
rows.fix: Gain trajectories become observable in the log and reproduced by replay, where the `Ref` writes were invisible to both.
rows.note: The spec does not claim the trace holds internal ports. Medium confidence; the text may use 'trace' loosely for the recorded session.

rows.claim: The reimplemented `PIVector` has an optional reset face that is sugar over the continuous-reset event
rows.evidence: No `PIVector` in src/. The shipped library has `PID` and `DiscretePID` (src/library.jl:2541, 2677) and no `reset` face on `PID`; the reset form exists only on DiscreteIntegrator and similar (src/library.jl:444-454, 559).
rows.fix: Name the library's vector PID, or say that a library PI component with a flag-gated reset face is the planned owner of the event.
rows.note: companions/migration_outline.md:71-72 and log D-141 (log.md:5292-5303) use the same name, so this is a planned item. The spec does not name `PIVector`. Verifier to rule whether a planned item may stay.

rows.claim: After the run, `TimeSeries` reads the retained snapshots
rows.evidence: No `TimeSeries` in src/. Post-run extraction is `series(sim, read_set)` returning a `Series` (src/sim.jl:2937, code_map.md src/sim.jl `series` entry). D-407 rejected FlightCore's `TimeSeries` (design/log.md:16818, 16841).
rows.fix: After the run, `series` gathers the logged snapshots into columns,
rows.note: The log retains snapshots at `log_every` and `log_max`, so 'retained' also means 'logged'.

ok.claim: Only event handlers write continuous x
`Simulation(world; Δt_frame = 1//50, algorithm = RK4())` is a valid call
Δt_base defaults to Δt_frame
The build pipeline runs at Simulation construction: probes, wiring checks, sort, rate compilation, layout
`init!(sim, condition; t0 = ...)` runs the stopped-sim services
`trim!(sim, problem; baseline, …)` is the trim service
The trim commit runs through the simulation's init!, the same boundary
init! establishes every root input's value (UninitializedInputs) and captures the trace header
The trim service writes root-input values it solved for via the condition
`attach!(sim, device, binding)` attaches a device

The output device runs a pure map_output on its own task

A claimed face that names no root input is refused at attach, with the face list in hand
A second joystick on the same faces is refused at attach (ClaimConflict)
A greedy binding claims every unclaimed face at the attach moment, never recomputed
`run!(sim; pace = 1, t_end = 1000)` is a valid call
The roster is frozen per run
A claim persists after the device's task exits, and the root input holds its last applied value
Recovery is stop, detach!, then init!, or replay! to the end then run! to continue
The trace can re-drive a fresh Simulation(world) bit-identically
